title: A free afternoon
prompt: You have a completely free afternoon with no obligations. Which plan sounds best?
intro: A free afternoon! Those are rare. What would you do with one?

choices.text: A beginner workshop where someone explains how everything works as you go.
choices.evidence: Preferred to understand a new activity while learning it.

choices.text: Going back to a place I already like and noticing something I missed before.
choices.evidence: Returned to something familiar to find more within it.

choices.text: A drop-in activity where I can experiment without committing to the whole day.
choices.evidence: Chose a low-pressure way to experiment independently.

choices.text: Joining friends for something none of us has tried before.
choices.evidence: Preferred discovering something new alongside other people.

title: The uncertain plan
prompt: You’re planning a day out, but one important detail is still uncertain. What do you do?
intro: The plan has a little gap in it. Plans do that sometimes.

choices.text: Compare the two most likely versions before choosing between them.
choices.evidence: Compared the likely possibilities before committing.

choices.text: Keep the confirmed parts of the plan and leave that time open for now.
choices.evidence: Protected what was already settled without forcing the missing detail.

choices.text: Choose an easy backup plan that we can change later if needed.
choices.evidence: Moved forward with a practical, reversible backup.

choices.text: Ask everyone going which option they would enjoy most.
choices.evidence: Made the uncertain part of the plan a shared decision.

title: What you keep
prompt: At the end of an ordinary week, you save one small thing to remember it by. What do you choose?
intro: These are things people left behind. Footprints, mostly. What would you leave to remember a week by?

choices.text: A question I kept thinking about, even though I never answered it.
choices.evidence: Kept an unresolved question as the week’s central memory.

choices.text: A tiny routine or detail that I might otherwise forget.
choices.evidence: Preserved an easily overlooked part of everyday life.

choices.text: A decision I made that changed how the week went.
choices.evidence: Focused on a moment of making a difference.

choices.text: A conversation or message from someone that stayed with me.
choices.evidence: Remembered the week through an interaction.

title: A last-minute invitation
prompt: You’ve planned a quiet afternoon for yourself. A friend suddenly invites you somewhere you’d probably enjoy. What do you do?
intro: Oh! A last-minute invitation. Those make the day wobble a little.

choices.text: Ask for a few more details before deciding which plan sounds better.
choices.evidence: Sought more context before choosing.

choices.text: Keep the afternoon I planned and suggest meeting another day.
choices.evidence: Protected an existing intention while leaving a future opening.

choices.text: Go with my friend. I can return to my original plan later.
choices.evidence: Accepted an opportunity while treating the original plan as recoverable.

choices.text: See whether we can meet for part of it so I still get some time to myself.
choices.evidence: Looked for a workable shared arrangement.

title: When something goes wrong
prompt: Your phone or laptop suddenly starts behaving strangely. What do you do first?
intro: It was working a moment ago. They’re rather dramatic, these little machines.

choices.text: Look up the symptoms and work out what probably caused the problem.
choices.evidence: Looked for an explanation before attempting a fix.

choices.text: Back up anything important before changing or restarting anything.
choices.evidence: Protected important information before trying to solve the problem.

choices.text: Try the quickest reversible fix and see what happens.
choices.evidence: Tested a practical fix that could easily be undone.

choices.text: Ask a friend who’s good with technology to look at it with me.
choices.evidence: Brought another person into solving the problem.

title: Same film, different view
prompt: You and a friend watch the same film. You love it; they don’t. What do you do next?
intro: Same film, two completely different reviews. That happens a lot here.

choices.text: Compare the scenes and details that each of us noticed most.
choices.evidence: Explored the observations behind different impressions.

choices.text: Leave it there. We can keep our different opinions without settling it.
choices.evidence: Preserved separate accounts without forcing resolution.

choices.text: Choose another film together and see whether our opinions line up next time.
choices.evidence: Used another experience to move beyond the disagreement.

choices.text: Ask what made the film land so differently for them.
choices.evidence: Prioritised the personal significance of another perspective.

title: A familiar place changes
prompt: A café, club or community space you love is getting a major redesign. What would you speak up for first?
intro: Here’s the old layout, and here’s the new one. They moved nearly everything.

choices.text: Explain what problem the redesign is meant to solve.
choices.evidence: Asked for the purpose and evidence behind a change.

choices.text: Keep one familiar feature that makes the place feel like itself.
choices.evidence: Protected a specific source of continuity.

choices.text: Try the new layout for a while before making it permanent.
choices.evidence: Favoured a practical, reversible trial.

choices.text: Let the regulars and staff help shape the redesign.
choices.evidence: Prioritised participation by the people affected.

title: One extra thing
prompt: You’re taking a day trip somewhere new with friends. The basics are packed. What extra do you bring?
intro: Everything we need is packed! There’s a little space left. Anything you’d like to bring?

choices.text: A guide or saved list, so we can understand what we find.
choices.evidence: Brought a resource for interpreting discoveries together.

choices.text: A notebook, so the little details don’t disappear when the day ends.
choices.evidence: Made room to retain details beyond the moment.

choices.text: A map with a few optional detours marked, in case something catches my eye.
choices.evidence: Kept room for self-directed exploration within a usable plan.

choices.text: A shared camera, so everyone can add what caught their eye.
choices.evidence: Chose a shared record that others could shape.
